# RmlUi + Lua Scene Integration

## Current architecture to reconcile (verify against source — may have moved)
- One Lua VM per scene: [src/LuaStateBootstrap.hpp](../../../src/LuaStateBootstrap.hpp)/.cpp sets
  up a fresh `lua_State*` per scene and hand-binds well over 100 ImGui functions
  (windows/layout/widgets/styling) directly onto it.
- Scenes pair a native C++ class in [src/scenes/](../../../src/scenes/) (e.g. `MainMenuScene`,
  `LobbyScene`, `PlayLevelScene`) with a Lua script in
  [assets/scenes/](../../../assets/scenes/) (e.g. `MainMenu.lua`, `Lobby.lua`, `PlayLevel.lua`).
- [src/utility/GameButton.hpp](../../../src/utility/GameButton.hpp) /
  `src/utility/GameImageButton.hpp` wrap ImGui buttons with hover/click sfx via `AudioEngine&`,
  exposed to Lua by handle.
- Lua binding metadata is generated by `python tools/gen_lua_metadata.py --source-root src --output
  assets/lua/meta/engine_globals.lua` — **must be re-run after any binding change** so editor
  tooling/autocomplete for scene scripts stays accurate.
- Lua version pinned in [CMakeLists.txt](../../../CMakeLists.txt) is `lua` v5.5 (via the `luasrc`
  FetchContent + hand-assembled static `lua` target at the bottom of the file) — **not** 5.1/LuaJIT.

## Open fact to confirm before designing anything (do not assume)
RmlUi's official Lua plugin (`RmlUi_Lua`) has historically targeted Lua 5.1/5.2-family APIs (and
LuaJIT). Whether it builds cleanly against Lua 5.5's C API is unverified — check the vendored
`build/_deps/rmlui-src`'s Lua plugin source (once fetched) for `lua_*`/`luaL_*` calls that were
removed/renamed in 5.4+/5.5 (e.g. `lua_objlen` vs `lua_rawlen`, changes to `lua_resume` signature,
`lua_Integer` handling) per the
[vendored-dependency-fact-check](../vendored-dependency-fact-check/SKILL.md) skill. If it doesn't
build against 5.5 as-is, options to raise with the user: patch the plugin locally, pin a different
Lua-plugin-compatible fork, or hand-write the RmlUi<->Lua binding surface needed (documents,
events, data bindings) instead of using the bundled plugin. Don't silently pick one — this is an
architecture decision to record once resolved (per the mode's step 7).

## Per-scene VM lifecycle question
Confirm whether `Rml::Lua::Initialise(lua_State*)` (or equivalent — verify exact call) can be
invoked once per already-existing per-scene `lua_State*` (keeping the current one-VM-per-scene
model), or whether the plugin expects to own/create the global Lua state itself. If it insists on
owning the state, that's a real conflict with the current architecture — surface it explicitly
rather than quietly changing the VM lifecycle; the mode instructions require documenting whichever
way this resolves.

## GameButton/GameImageButton replacement shape
Not a 1:1 port. Likely shape once resolved:
- `.rml` markup defines the button element (e.g. a styled `<button>` or `<div>` with an `onclick`
  handler) per scene.
- `.rcss` supplies the persistent visual styling (hover/active states) that ImGui's per-call
  styling API previously handled in C++/Lua.
- Click/hover **sound** hookup still goes through the existing `AudioEngine` — RmlUi doesn't know
  about audio, so scene-side C++ (or a Lua event handler calling back into a bound `AudioEngine`
  play function) still wires `hoverSoundPath_`/`clickSoundPath_`-equivalent behavior via RmlUi
  event listeners (`mouseover`/`click`) rather than ImGui's per-frame `IsItemHovered()` polling.

## Procedure
1. Resolve the Lua-5.5-compatibility question first (blocks everything else in this skill).
2. Decide and document the VM lifecycle answer.
3. Prototype one scene's buttons (start with SplashScreen or MainMenu, per the mode's scene order)
   as `.rml`/`.rcss` + event-listener-driven sfx before generalizing a `GameButton`-equivalent
   helper.
4. Remove only the ImGui Lua bindings in `LuaStateBootstrap.cpp` that the migrated scene actually
   used — leave bindings for not-yet-migrated scenes intact.
5. Regenerate `assets/lua/meta/engine_globals.lua` via `tools/gen_lua_metadata.py` after binding
   changes.
